analysis: The PR changes documentation only: docs/developer/test.md adds a 'Prompt Preparation And Admission' test section (head lines 322-341), and docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds one benchmark table row for `--prompt-prep` (head line 572). The supplied head_text for test.md covers lines 484-1015 and does not include the added section itself; I reviewed that section through the patch excerpt. I traced the new content against the threat model. The test section describes synthetic tokenizers loaded through LocalTokenizerLoader with no download, an optional PROMPT_TOKEN_CACHE_MODEL_DIRS variable pointing at local model directories, and a CPU-only benchmark that loads only the tokenizer. None of this changes runtime code, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, the coordinator WebSocket contract, or encrypted prefix-cache storage (T-041). No secrets or credentials are introduced, and no new network or telemetry paths are documented. The `--prompt-prep` benchmark prints JSON containing timings and difference indicators. The docs do not say whether prompt content is emitted, so the implementation in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift is unsupplied. The next pass should check that the report never includes prompt text or tokens. This matters because the docs elsewhere forbid sending tokens, prompts or completions to telemetry. The docs also mention a prompt token cache (PromptTokenCacheTests), and its implementation is not in this batch. If that cache is new runtime code, it could affect the cross-tenant, TTFT and at-rest analysis in T-041. The supplied evidence is docs only, so I record this as an open integration question rather than a finding. The unchanged portions of cli-reference.md (base lines 1-404) were reviewed for context and show no regression.
